title: 1962 AHSME Problem 23
statement: In triangle \(ABC,\) \(CD\) is the altitude to \(AB\) and \(AE\) is the altitude to \(BC.\) If the lengths of \(AB,\) \(CD,\) and \(AE\) are known, the length of \(DB\) is:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: not determined by the information given

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: determined only if \(A\) is an acute angle

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: determined only if \(B\) is an acute angle

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: determined only if \(ABC\) is an acute triangle

solutions.text:
Let \(AB=c,\) \(CD=h,\) and \(AE=e.\) Equating two area formulas gives \[ \frac12ch=\frac12(BC)e, \] so \(BC=\frac{ch}{e}.\) Since triangle \(BCD\) is right at \(D,\) \[ DB=\sqrt{BC^2-CD^2}. \] This determines \(DB\) whether the original triangle is acute, right, or obtuse, so none of the first four choices is correct.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Compute the triangle’s area in two ways using the two known altitudes
